overall: The AG found the Wayland Select Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the open-session topic was not discussed so its notice could not be insufficient, and the executive session notice and discussion were adequate.

allegations.summary: Open-session notice topic on a public records reconsideration determination was alleged to be too vague to tell the public what would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, since the Board did not actually discuss this topic, we find that the notice was not insufficient with respect to this particular topic.

allegations.summary: Executive session notice topic (Purpose 7, reviewing and possibly releasing Galbi litigation minutes) was alleged to be insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: as it indicated to the public the executive session purpose for which it intended to convene— Purpose 7—and specifically listed the meeting dates of the minutes it planned to review for public disclosure.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session's true purpose was to respond to a public records determination, not the minutes review listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the discussions were appropriate as the Board was instructed in the determination letter to clarify whether the minutes could remain redacted to protect privileged attorney-client communications.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
